introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II and Task III) specified in the question paper.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 23/0595/3/Grp 1 to Grp 4); a candidate sits only ONE group. Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing), Task II (spreadsheet) and Task III (a short exercise on HTML, on a database or on a C or Pascal program). The working files named in the tasks (the picture UN.jpg, the pictures of the authors) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

incertitudes: Structure du lot : les quatre PDF fournis sont nommes DAY1 a DAY4, mais les pages de garde imprimees parlent de GROUPES (« Group Two », « Group Three », « Group Four », livrets 23/0595/3/Grp 2, 3 et 4), pas de jours. Un seul dossier, douze fichiers : numero_exercice G1-T1 a G4-T3 (groupe n, tache m), groupes ["GROUP 1"] a ["GROUP 4"] (et non D<n>-T<m> / ["DAY n"]). regles_choix est vide : le candidat ne passe qu'un seul groupe, ce qui n'est pas exprimable.

Le PDF DAY1 (Group One) n'a que 3 pages et pas de page de garde (il commence a la page 2 du livret, « Do all the tasks... ») : le niveau et la matiere sont verifies par la reference imprimee en pied de page (0000/0595/3/Grp 1, soit le code 0595) et par la structure identique aux trois autres groupes. La duree de 2 h 30 est reprise des pages de garde des groupes 2, 3 et 4 (« Two and a Half hours »).

Aucun corrige officiel n'existe : les reponses sont redigees. Les « marking ideas » sont des repartitions indicatives faites d'apres les points imprimes ; le bareme du jury n'est pas connu. Les fichiers de donnees du jour (image UN.jpg, photos des auteurs, dossier du candidat) ne sont pas dans le PDF ; aucun logiciel (traitement de texte, tableur, gestionnaire de base de donnees, navigateur, compilateur) n'a ete execute : les menus sont donnes sous leur forme generale (Office / LibreOffice recents), de memoire, sans version de logiciel affirmee.

Les filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo), les cadres d'en-tete (numero de centre, nom du candidat, « For examiners' use only »), les lignes a completer et les artefacts du scanner (scans sans couche texte, photos de feuilles legerement inclinees) sont ignores. Chaque PDF a ete lu page par page en image.

Tous les resultats chiffres (colonnes calculees, classements, comptages, totaux) ont ete recalcules avec Python a partir des donnees imprimees, en fractions exactes pour les moyennes ; les formules de tableur ont ete traduites en Python (SUM, AVERAGE, RANK, IF, COUNTIF). Les points imprimes de chaque tache somment bien au total annonce (voir ci-dessous) ; aucun point imprime n'a ete corrige.

Group Four, Task II : points imprimes 4, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 2, 3 = 20, comme annonce. Numerotation imprimee « 1. 1. » en tete et « Save your work as Task 2 and print » dans la question 9 : repris. La question 6 porte 2 points (formule et copie) puis 1 point (ecrire la formule en B10) : transcrite en 6a et 6b. La question 8 dit « the number of boys in cells A14 » : A14 contient l'etiquette « No boys », la cellule vide du resultat est A15 (comme B15 pour les filles) : lecture retenue A15, signalee dans le corrige.

Figure 2 (page 3 du PDF DAY4) : extraite sans filigrane, controle OCR OK. Lue : bonus H2 = 2, coefficient H3 = 3 ; Score 1 = 7, 15, 6, 14, 6, 9 ; Score 2 = 8, 18, 12, 12, 14, 7 ; genres F, F, F, M, M, F. Les cellules « passed » (F14) et « Failed » (G14) servent aux commentaires. Resultats recalcules avec Python : moyennes 7,5 / 16,5 / 9 / 13 / 10 / 8 ; scores finaux 9,5 / 18,5 / 11 / 15 / 12 / 10 (donc 1 echec : Orock Justine) ; final x coefficient 28,5 / 55,5 / 33 / 45 / 36 / 30 ; 4 filles et 2 garcons. Le coefficient H3 n'est utilise que par la ligne 11 (le sujet ne precise pas son role : lecture « Final Score * Coefficient » = ligne 11).

questions.corrige_markdown:
Open a new workbook and key in the data in the cells shown.

1. Title in A1, the bonus mark 2 in H2 and the coefficient 3 in H3 (with their labels).
2. The six names in B4:G4, the genders in B5:G5 (F, F, F, M, M, F), Score 1 in B6:G6 and Score 2 in B7:G7.
3. The row labels in column A (rows 4 to 11) and the two small boxes at the bottom (labels in row 13 and row 14).
4. Check every value, then add borders and bold labels as in the figure.

Marking idea (4 marks): title, bonus and coefficient (1); names and genders (1); Score 1 and Score 2 (1); labels and the two boxes (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Enter in cell B8, the formula that computes the average mark of Orock Justine. Extend this formula to the appropriate cells. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In **B8** type **`=AVERAGE(B6:B7)`** (or `=(B6+B7)/2`): the average of Score 1 (7) and Score 2 (8) is $\frac{7 + 8}{2} = 7.5$. Then drag the fill handle to the right, from B8 to G8: the column letter changes by itself.

Results for B8:G8: 7.5, 16.5, 9, 13, 10, 8 (Orock Justine, Assamba Jane, Wafo Grace, Nfor Jones, Jean Alain, Siewe Delphine).

Marking idea (2 marks): correct formula for B8 (1); copied to C8:G8 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Write the formula in B8 on the space below. *[1 mark]*
The final score of each student is obtained by adding the bonus mark in cell H2 to all the students. Compute the final score of Orock Justine, then extend this formula to the others. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The final score is the average plus the bonus mark. The bonus mark is stored once in H2, so it must be fixed with an **absolute reference**:

**B9: `=B8+$H$2`**

For Orock Justine: $7.5 + 2 = 9.5$. Copy B9 to the right as far as G9. Results for B9:G9: 9.5, 18.5, 11, 15, 12, 10.

Without the dollar signs, the formula copied to C9 would become `=C8+I2`, which is wrong (an empty cell).

Marking idea (2 marks): average plus bonus (1); absolute reference to H2 and copied to G9 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Write the formula you used in the space below. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**B9: `=B8+$H$2`**

Marking idea (1 mark): the formula of question 4.

questions.enonce_markdown: The comments for a student can either be the value in cell F14 or that in G14. Use the IF function to compute the comment for Orock Justine, then extend the formula to the other cells. A student has passed if his final score is greater than or equal to 10. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The comment is the word of the cell F14 ("passed") if the final score is at least 10, and the word of the cell G14 ("Failed") otherwise. These two cells are fixed with dollar signs because they do not change from one student to another:

**B10: `=IF(B9>=10,$F$14,$G$14)`**

Copy it to the right as far as G10. Results for B10:G10:

| Student | Final score | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Orock Justine | 9.5 | Failed |
| Assamba Jane | 18.5 | passed |
| Wafo Grace | 11 | passed |
| Nfor Jones | 15 | passed |
| Jean Alain | 12 | passed |
| Siewe Delphine | 10 | passed |

"Greater than or equal to 10" is written `>=10`: Siewe Delphine, with exactly 10, has passed.

Marking idea (2 marks): IF with the condition B9>=10 and the two cells F14 and G14 (1); formula copied with correct results (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Write the formula you used in cell B10 in the space below. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**B10: `=IF(B9>=10,$F$14,$G$14)`**. (A formula that writes the words directly, `=IF(B9>=10,"passed","Failed")`, gives the same results.)

Marking idea (1 mark): the formula of question 6a.

questions.enonce_markdown: Enter in cell B11 the formula to compute the final score of Orock Justine in the space below. Copy the formula to the corresponding cells for the other students. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The row 11 is "Final Score * Coefficient": the final score (row 9) is multiplied by the coefficient stored in H3 (fixed with dollar signs):

**B11: `=B9*$H$3`**

For Orock Justine: $9.5 \times 3 = 28.5$. Copy B11 to G11. Results for B11:G11: 28.5, 55.5, 33, 45, 36, 30.

Marking idea (2 marks): final score multiplied by the coefficient with `$H$3` (1); copied to G11 with correct values (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Use the COUNTIF function to compute the number of girls in cell B15 and the number of boys in cells A14. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
COUNTIF counts the cells of a range that are equal to a given value. The gender is in B5:G5 (F for a girl, M for a boy):

- **B15** (number of girls, under "No girls"): **`=COUNTIF($B$5:$G$5,"F")`** gives **4** (Orock Justine, Assamba Jane, Wafo Grace, Siewe Delphine).
- **A15** (number of boys, under "No boys"): **`=COUNTIF($B$5:$G$5,"M")`** gives **2** (Nfor Jones, Jean Alain).

Check: $4 + 2 = 6$, the number of students. The printed question says "cells A14", but A14 holds the label "No boys": the empty cell for the result is A15, under the label.

Marking idea (2 marks): COUNTIF for girls, result 4 (1); COUNTIF for boys, result 2 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Represent the data "name of student" and "final score" on a bar chart. Save your work as Task 2 and print. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Select the names B4:G4, then hold the *Ctrl* key and select the final scores B9:G9.
2. *Insert* > **Charts** > **Column** (or *Bar*) > *Clustered Column*.
3. Add a title (for example "Final scores of the students"), a title for each axis (horizontal: "Name of student"; vertical: "Final score") and check that each bar is labelled with a student's name.
4. Data used by the chart: Orock Justine 9.5; Assamba Jane 18.5; Wafo Grace 11; Nfor Jones 15; Jean Alain 12; Siewe Delphine 10.
5. *File* > *Save As* > **Task 2**, then *File* > *Print* (check the preview: the table and the chart on the page).

Marking idea (3 marks): right data selected, names on one axis and final scores on the other (1); a bar chart with the six bars at the right heights (1); title and labelled axes (1).
